source: How many ways to cut a square into 4 equal areas?
videos.handover: The first idea opens: count unit squares to compare two rangoli rectangles.
videos.note: The chapter opener: how many ways can a square be cut into 4 parts of equal area? Left open.

source: A rangoli artist has a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle and an 8 cm by

items.question: A rangoli artist has a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle and an 8 cm by 3 cm rectangle. Which needs more powder?
steps: Count unit squares in the first: 7 × 4 = 28.
Count unit squares in the second: 8 × 3 = 24.
28 is more than 24.
items.answer: The 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle needs more powder: 28 cm² against 24 cm²

videos.answer: The 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle needs more powder: 28 cm² against 24 cm²

source: A diagonal is drawn in a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle. Find the ar

items.question: A diagonal is drawn in a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle. Find the area of each triangle.
steps: The rectangle has area 7 × 4 = 28 cm².
The diagonal makes two congruent triangles.
Each triangle is 1/2 × 28 = 14 cm².
items.answer: Each triangle has area 14 cm²

videos.answer: Each triangle has area 14 cm²

source: Compare a 10 cm by 1 cm strip with a 5 cm by 4 cm rectangle:

items.question: Compare a 10 cm by 1 cm strip with a 5 cm by 4 cm rectangle: perimeter and area.
steps: Strip perimeter: 2 × (10 + 1) = 22 cm. Strip area: 10 × 1 = 10 cm².
Rectangle perimeter: 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 cm. Rectangle area: 5 × 4 = 20 cm².
items.answer: The strip has the larger perimeter (22 cm) but the smaller area (10 cm²)

videos.answer: The strip has the larger perimeter (22 cm) but the smaller area (10 cm²)

source: Compare a 4 by 4 square with a thin zigzag made of 9 unit sq

items.question: Compare a 4 by 4 square with a thin zigzag made of 9 unit squares joined edge to edge in one line with bends.
steps: Square: perimeter 4 × 4 = 16 units, area 16 square units.
Zigzag: each square shares edges with its neighbours, leaving 2 × 9 + 2 = 20 unit edges on the boundary, so perimeter 20 units.
Zigzag area: 9 square units.
items.answer: The zigzag has the larger perimeter (20 units against 16) but the smaller area (9 against 16)

videos.answer: The zigzag has the larger perimeter (20 units against 16) but the smaller area (9 against 16)

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 1)

items.question: Identify the missing sidelengths. (i) A plus shaped figure is made of four rectangles: a 28 in² piece whose right edge rises 4 in above a 21 in² piece of length 7 in, a 35 in² piece of width 3 in plus the width of the 28 in² piece, and a 14 in² strip that hangs 2 in below the 35 in² piece; find the width of the 14 in² strip. (ii) A 29 m² piece and an 11 m² piece are both 4 m tall, and the bold rectangle made of the 29 m² piece and the piece below it has area 50 m²; find the missing sides.
steps: (i) The 21 in² piece is 7 in long, so its height is 21 ÷ 7 = 3 in.
The 28 in² piece is 4 + 3 = 7 in tall, so its width is 28 ÷ 7 = 4 in.
The 35 in² piece is 3 + 4 = 7 in wide, so its height is 35 ÷ 7 = 5 in.
The 14 in² strip is 5 + 2 = 7 in tall, so its width is 14 ÷ 7 = 2 in.
(ii) Top widths: 29 ÷ 4 = 7.25 m and 11 ÷ 4 = 2.75 m.
The lower piece has area 50 − 29 = 21 m² and width 7.25 m, so its height is 21 ÷ 7.25 ≈ 2.9 m.
items.answer: (i) 2 in, with 3 in, 4 in and 5 in on the way. (ii) 7.25 m and 2.75 m across the top, and a lower height of 84/29 m, about 2.9 m

videos.answer: (i) 2 in, with 3 in, 4 in and 5 in on the way. (ii) 7.25 m and 2.75 m across the top, and a lower height of 84/29 m, about 2.9 m

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 2)

items.question: A path (the shaded portion) is laid around a rectangular park EFGH inside a rectangle ABCD. (i) What measurements do you need to find the area of the path? Assign values and give a formula. (ii) If the width of the path along each side is given, can you find its area? If not, what else do you need? (iii) Does the area of the path change when the outer rectangle is moved while keeping the park inside it?
steps: (i) Measure the length and width of ABCD and of EFGH.
Area of path = area of ABCD − area of EFGH. With ABCD 20 m by 14 m and EFGH 16 m by 10 m: 20 × 14 − 16 × 10 = 280 − 160 = 120 m².

(ii) The widths alone are not enough; we also need the park's length and width. With a park 16 m by 10 m and widths 2 m on every side, break the path into two long strips 20 m by 2 m and two short strips 10 m by 2 m: 2 × 40 + 2 × 20 = 120 m².
(iii) Moving ABCD around the park changes the widths but not the two rectangles, so the path area stays the same.
items.answer: (i) Path area = area of ABCD − area of EFGH (120 m² for the chosen values). (ii) Also need the park's sides; same 120 m². (iii) No, the area does not change

videos.answer: (i) Path area = area of ABCD − area of EFGH (120 m² for the chosen values). (ii) Also need the park's sides; same 120 m². (iii) No, the area does not change

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 3)

items.question: A plot has sides 14 m and 12 m with a crosspath. What other measurements do you need to find the area of the crosspath? Assign values and give a formula.
steps: We need the widths of the two paths: p for the path along the 14 m side and q for the path along the 12 m side.
The two strips are 14 × p and 12 × q, but they overlap in a p by q square counted twice.
items.answer: The widths of the two paths; area = 14p + 12q − pq, which is 36 m² when the widths are 1 m and 2 m

videos.answer: The widths of the two paths; area = 14p + 12q − pq, which is 36 m² when the widths are 1 m and 2 m

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 4)

items.question: Find the area of the spiral tube shown in the figure. The tube has the same width (1 unit) throughout, and its straight parts measure 20, 20, 20, 15, 15, 10, 10, 5 and 5 along the outside.
steps: The hint: an L shaped tube with arms 5 and 5 has the same area as a straight tube of length 5 + 5 − 1 = 9, because the corner square is counted in both arms.
Add all the straight lengths: 20 + 20 + 20 + 15 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 5 = 120.
There are 8 bends, each counted twice, so subtract 8: 120 − 8 = 112.
The straightened tube is 112 units long and 1 unit wide: 112 × 1 = 112.
items.answer: 112 square units

videos.answer: 112 square units

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 5)

items.question: A square is divided into regions 1, 2 and 3. If the sidelength of the square is doubled, what is the increase in the areas of the regions 1, 2 and 3? Give reasons.
steps: Doubling the side doubles every length in the figure, both across and up.
Each region's area is multiplied by 2 × 2 = 4.
So each region grows by 4 − 1 = 3 times its old area.
items.answer: Each region becomes 4 times as big, an increase of 3 times its original area

videos.answer: Each region becomes 4 times as big, an increase of 3 times its original area

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 6)

items.question: Divide a square into 4 parts by drawing two perpendicular lines inside the square, then rearrange the pieces to get a larger square with a hole inside.
steps: Draw two perpendicular lines through the square that are not parallel to its sides; the 4 pieces are congruent.
Turn the pieces so that each right angle points outward and the long edges run round the outside.
The outside forms a bigger square; the gap in the middle is a small square hole.
The area of the big square minus the hole equals the area of the original square.
items.answer: The 4 congruent pieces form a larger square around a square hole; total area is unchanged

videos.answer: The 4 congruent pieces form a larger square around a square hole; total area is unchanged

source: X is on the top side of a rectangle with DC = 5 cm and heigh

items.question: X is on the top side of a rectangle with DC = 5 cm and height 4 cm. Find the area of ΔXDC.
steps: Drop the altitude XY to DC. It splits the rectangle into two rectangles.
Each small rectangle is cut in half by XD or XC.
So ΔXDC is half of the whole rectangle: 1/2 × 5 × 4 = 10 cm².
items.answer: 10 cm²

videos.answer: 10 cm²

source: A triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.

items.question: A triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.
steps: Its outer rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm, area 8 × 5 = 40 cm².
The triangle is half of it.
items.answer: 20 cm²

videos.answer: 20 cm²

source: In an obtuse triangle ABC the height from A meets CB extende

items.question: In an obtuse triangle ABC the height from A meets CB extended at D, with h = 4 cm, DB = 3 cm and BC = 6 cm. Find the area.
steps: DC = DB + BC = 3 + 6 = 9 cm.
Area of ΔADC = 1/2 × 4 × 9 = 18 cm². Area of ΔADB = 1/2 × 4 × 3 = 6 cm².
Area of ΔABC = 18 − 6 = 12 cm², and 1/2 × 4 × 6 = 12 cm² too.
items.answer: 12 cm², the same as 1/2 × base × height

videos.answer: 12 cm², the same as 1/2 × base × height

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 1)

items.question: Find the areas of the following triangles: (i) base BC with 4 cm marked and height AE = 3 cm, (ii) base EF = 5 cm with height DN = 3.2 cm, (iii) right triangle NAT with NA = 4 cm and AT = 3 cm.
steps: (ii) The height DN is drawn to EF, so 1/2 × 5 × 3.2 = 8 cm².
(iii) The two legs are a base and its height: 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm².
items.answer: (i) 6 cm² (ii) 8 cm² (iii) 6 cm²

videos.answer: (i) 6 cm² (ii) 8 cm² (iii) 6 cm²

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 3)

items.question: Find the area of ΔSUB, given that it is isosceles, SE is perpendicular to UB, and the area of ΔSEB is 24 sq. units.
steps: In an isosceles triangle the perpendicular from S to UB meets it at its midpoint, so UE = EB.
ΔSUE and ΔSEB have the same base length and the same height SE, so equal areas.
Area of ΔSUB = 24 + 24 = 48 sq. units.
items.answer: 48 sq. units

videos.answer: 48 sq. units

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 4)

items.question: [Śulba-Sūtras] Give a method to transform a rectangle into a triangle of equal area.
steps: Take rectangle ABCD with base AB and height BC.
Extend AB to E so that BE = AB. Then AE is twice the base.
Join E to D. Triangle AED has base 2 × AB and height AD, so its area is 1/2 × 2AB × AD = AB × AD.
Another way: cut the rectangle along a diagonal and place the two halves side by side along the height to form one triangle.
items.answer: A triangle on double the base with the same height (or double the height on the same base) has the rectangle's area

videos.answer: A triangle on double the base with the same height (or double the height on the same base) has the rectangle's area

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 5)

items.question: [Śulba-Sūtras] Give a method to transform a triangle into a rectangle of equal area.
steps: Draw the height AX of triangle ABC on base BC.
Mark the midpoints of AB and AC and join them; this line is parallel to BC at half the height.
Drop perpendiculars from the two midpoints to BC. Cut off the two small top triangles and turn each into the gap below it.
The result is a rectangle with base BC and height 1/2 AX, so its area is 1/2 × BC × AX.
items.answer: Cut along the line joining the midpoints of the two sides and swing the top pieces down: a rectangle on the same base with half the height

videos.answer: Cut along the line joining the midpoints of the two sides and swing the top pieces down: a rectangle on the same base with half the height

source: In ΔABC, AX = 3 is the height to BC = 5, and AC = 4. Find th

items.question: In ΔABC, AX = 3 is the height to BC = 5, and AC = 4. Find the height BY to AC.
steps: Area = 1/2 × 3 × 5 = 7.5 square units.
Also, area = 1/2 × 4 × BY, which is 2 × BY.
So 2 × BY = 7.5, and BY = 7.5 ÷ 2 = 3.75 units.
items.answer: BY = 3.75 units

videos.answer: BY = 3.75 units

source: The diagonals of an 8 cm by 6 cm rectangle meet at O. Find t

items.question: The diagonals of an 8 cm by 6 cm rectangle meet at O. Find the area of each of the four triangles.
steps: The rectangle has area 8 × 6 = 48 cm².
Adjacent triangles have equal halves of a diagonal as bases and the same height, so equal areas.
All four are equal: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm².
items.answer: Each triangle is 12 cm², even though they are not congruent

videos.answer: Each triangle is 12 cm², even though they are not congruent

source: BC = 6 cm and line l is parallel to BC, 4 cm away. Find the

items.question: BC = 6 cm and line l is parallel to BC, 4 cm away. Find the area of a triangle on BC with its top on l, and say how it changes as the top moves.
steps: Base = 6 cm, height = 4 cm for every position of the top.
Moving the top changes the slanting sides, not the height.
items.answer: Always 12 cm²: equal areas; only the perimeter changes

videos.answer: Always 12 cm²: equal areas; only the perimeter changes

source: B and C are 3 cm below line l and BC = 8 cm. Find the smalle

items.question: B and C are 3 cm below line l and BC = 8 cm. Find the smallest possible value of AB + AC with A on l.
steps: Reflect C in l: C′ is 3 cm above l, so 6 cm above the line BC, directly over C.
BC′ is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 8 and 6: √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10.
The straight line BC′ crosses l halfway across, above the midpoint of BC.
items.answer: The smallest AB + AC is 10 cm, with A on the perpendicular bisector of BC

videos.answer: The smallest AB + AC is 10 cm, with A on the perpendicular bisector of BC

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 2)

items.question: Find the length of the altitude BY in ΔABC, where AX = 4 units is the height to BC = 6 units and AC = 8 units.
steps: Area = 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12 square units.
Also area = 1/2 × 8 × BY, which is 4 × BY.
4 × BY = 12, so BY = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 units.
items.answer: BY = 3 units

videos.answer: BY = 3 units

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 6)

items.question: ABCD, BCEF and BFGH are identical squares, with H directly above B. The red region is the triangle DCH and the blue region is the part of square ABCD to the left of the line DH. (i) If the area of the red region is 49 sq. units, what is the area of the blue region? (ii) In another version, if the blue and red regions together are 180 sq. units, what is the area of each square?
steps: Let each square have side s. Red: base DC = s, height CH = 2s, so area 1/2 × s × 2s, which is s².
DH rises 2s over a run of s, so it crosses AB at its midpoint: the blue triangle has legs s and s/2, area one quarter of s².
(i) s² = 49, so blue = 49 ÷ 4 = 12.25 sq. units.
(ii) Blue + red is five quarters of s², so s² = 180 × 4 ÷ 5 = 144 sq. units.
items.answer: (i) 12.25 sq. units (ii) 144 sq. units

videos.answer: (i) 12.25 sq. units (ii) 144 sq. units

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 7)

items.question: If M and N are the midpoints of XY and XZ, what fraction of the area of ΔXYZ is the area of ΔXMN? (Hint: join NY.)
steps: NY is a median of ΔXYZ (N is the midpoint of XZ), so ΔXNY is half of ΔXYZ.
In ΔXNY, NM is a median (M is the midpoint of XY), so ΔXMN is half of ΔXNY.
items.answer: ΔXMN is 1/4 of ΔXYZ

videos.answer: ΔXMN is 1/4 of ΔXYZ

source: Figure it Out (triangles, question 8)

items.question: Gopal needs to carry water from the river to his water tank. He starts from his house. What is the shortest path from his house to the river and then to the water tank? Recreate the map and trace it.
steps: Treat the river bank as a mirror line and reflect the water tank to the far side of it.
Join the house to the reflected tank with a straight line.
Where this line meets the river bank is the best point to fill water.
Walk house to that point, then to the real tank: this is as long as the straight line, the shortest possible.
items.answer: Reflect the tank in the river bank; the straight line from the house to the reflection meets the bank at the best point

videos.answer: Reflect the tank in the river bank; the straight line from the house to the reflection meets the bank at the best point

source: A quadrilateral ABCD has diagonal BD = 10 cm. The heights fr

items.question: A quadrilateral ABCD has diagonal BD = 10 cm. The heights from A and C to BD are 4 cm and 3 cm. Find its area.
steps: Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × 10 × 4 = 20 cm².
Area of ΔBCD = 1/2 × 10 × 3 = 15 cm².
Area of ABCD = 20 + 15 = 35 cm².
items.answer: 35 cm²

videos.answer: 35 cm²

source: A pentagon is a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a triangle of he

items.question: A pentagon is a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with a triangle of height 3 cm on its 6 cm side. Find its area.
steps: Rectangle: 6 × 4 = 24 cm².
Triangle: 1/2 × 6 × 3 = 9 cm².
Pentagon: 24 + 9 = 33 cm².
items.answer: 33 cm²

videos.answer: 33 cm²

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 1)

items.question: Find the area of the quadrilateral ABCD given that AC = 22 cm, BM = 3 cm, DN = 3 cm, BM is perpendicular to AC, and DN is perpendicular to AC.
steps: The diagonal AC splits ABCD into ΔABC and ΔACD.
Area of ΔABC = 1/2 × 22 × 3 = 33 cm². Area of ΔACD = 1/2 × 22 × 3 = 33 cm².
Area of ABCD = 33 + 33 = 66 cm².
items.answer: 66 cm²

videos.answer: 66 cm²

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 2)

items.question: Find the area of the shaded region FECD given that ABCD is a rectangle, with AB = 18 cm, BC = 10 cm, AE = 10 cm, EB = 8 cm, AF = 6 cm and FD = 4 cm.
steps: Rectangle ABCD: 18 × 10 = 180 cm².
Unshaded ΔAEF: 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². Unshaded ΔEBC: 1/2 × 8 × 10 = 40 cm².
Shaded region = 180 − 30 − 40 = 110 cm².
items.answer: 110 cm²

videos.answer: 110 cm²

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 3)

items.question: What measurements would you need to find the area of a regular hexagon?
steps: Join the centre to all six corners: six identical equilateral triangles.
Each triangle has a side of the hexagon as base and the distance from the centre to that side as height.
So the side length and the centre to side distance are enough: area = 6 × 1/2 × side × that distance.
items.answer: The side length and the perpendicular distance from the centre to a side

videos.answer: The side length and the perpendicular distance from the centre to a side

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 4)

items.question: What fraction of the total area of the rectangle is the area of the blue region? (Two blue triangles stand on the top and bottom sides of the rectangle, with their tips meeting at a point inside.)
steps: Each blue triangle has a full side of the rectangle as base: the length L.
Their heights, from the shared point to the top and to the bottom, add up to the width W.
items.answer: Half of the rectangle is blue

videos.answer: Half of the rectangle is blue

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 5)

items.question: Give a method to obtain a quadrilateral whose area is half that of a given quadrilateral.
steps: Mark the midpoints of the four sides and join them in order.
Each corner triangle cut off is one quarter of the triangle made by a diagonal (both sides are halved).
The four corners together are one quarter of each pair of diagonal triangles, so half the quadrilateral; the inner quadrilateral is the other half.
items.answer: Join the midpoints of the sides in order; the inner quadrilateral has half the area

videos.answer: Join the midpoints of the sides in order; the inner quadrilateral has half the area

source: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 5 cm. Cut and slide

items.question: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 5 cm. Cut and slide it into a rectangle and find its area.
steps: Cut along a height of 5 cm and slide the triangle across.
The rectangle is 9 cm long and 5 cm high.
Area = 9 × 5 = 45 cm².
items.answer: 45 cm², the same as the parallelogram

videos.answer: 45 cm², the same as the parallelogram

source: A parallelogram has sides 10 cm and 6 cm. The height on the

items.question: A parallelogram has sides 10 cm and 6 cm. The height on the 10 cm side is 4.8 cm. Find the area and the height on the 6 cm side.
steps: With base 6 cm: 6 × height = 48.
Height = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm.
items.answer: Area 48 cm²; the height on the 6 cm side is 8 cm

videos.answer: Area 48 cm²; the height on the 6 cm side is 8 cm

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 1)

items.question: Observe the parallelograms (a) to (g) drawn on a grid, all on equal bases between the same two grid lines. (i) What can we say about the areas of all these parallelograms? (ii) What can we say about their perimeters? Which figure appears to have the maximum perimeter, and which has the minimum perimeter?
steps: (i) Each has the same base and the same height, so each has the same area, base × height.
(ii) The perimeter is twice the base plus twice the slanting side.
The more a parallelogram leans, the longer its slanting sides, so the larger its perimeter.
items.answer: (i) All have equal areas. (ii) The perimeters differ: (g), leaning most, appears largest and (a), almost upright, smallest

videos.answer: (i) All have equal areas. (ii) The perimeters differ: (g), leaning most, appears largest and (a), almost upright, smallest

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 2)

items.question: Find the areas of the following parallelograms: (i) base 7 cm, height 4 cm, (ii) base 5 cm, height 3 cm, (iii) side 5 cm with height 4.8 cm drawn to it, (iv) side 2 cm with height 4.4 cm drawn to it.
items.answer: (i) 28 cm² (ii) 15 cm² (iii) 24 cm² (iv) 8.8 cm²

videos.answer: (i) 28 cm² (ii) 15 cm² (iii) 24 cm² (iv) 8.8 cm²

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 3)

items.question: Find QN in parallelogram PQRS, where SR = 12 cm, the height QM to SR is 6 cm, PS = 7.6 cm, and QN is perpendicular to PS.
steps: Area = SR × QM = 12 × 6 = 72 cm².
Also area = PS × QN = 7.6 × QN.
items.answer: QN ≈ 9.47 cm

videos.answer: QN ≈ 9.47 cm

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 4)

items.question: Consider a rectangle and a parallelogram of the same sidelengths: 5 cm and 4 cm. Which has the greater area? (Hint: imagine constructing them on the same base.)
steps: Rectangle: 5 × 4 = 20 cm².
On the same 5 cm base, the parallelogram's height is shorter than its slanting 4 cm side.
So its area, 5 × height, is less than 20 cm².
items.answer: The rectangle has the greater area

videos.answer: The rectangle has the greater area

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 5)

items.question: Give a method to obtain a rectangle whose area is twice that of a given triangle. What are the different methods that you can think of?
steps: Method 1: draw a line through the top vertex parallel to the base and perpendiculars to the base at its ends; the rectangle on the base and height is twice the triangle.
Method 2: take two copies of the triangle, join them into a parallelogram, then cut and slide it into a rectangle.
Either way the rectangle is base × height, twice 1/2 × base × height.
items.answer: Build the rectangle on the base and height, or join two copies into a parallelogram and cut and slide

videos.answer: Build the rectangle on the base and height, or join two copies into a parallelogram and cut and slide

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 6)

items.question: [Śulba-Sūtras] Give a method to obtain a rectangle of the same area as a given triangle.
steps: Join the midpoints of the two sides; this line is parallel to the base at half the height.
Drop perpendiculars from these midpoints to the base.
Cut off the two small top pieces and turn each down into the gap below it.
The result is a rectangle with the same base and half the height: 1/2 × base × height.
items.answer: Cut at half the height and swing the top pieces down: a rectangle on the base with half the height

videos.answer: Cut at half the height and swing the top pieces down: a rectangle on the base with half the height

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 7)

items.question: [Śulba-Sūtras] An isosceles triangle can be converted into a rectangle by dissection in a simpler way. Can you find out how to do it? (Hint: show that ΔADB and ΔADC can be made into halves of a rectangle.)
steps: The altitude AD of isosceles ΔABC meets BC at its midpoint, giving two congruent right triangles.
Turn ΔADC over and place it against ΔADB with the hypotenuses together.
The two right triangles form a rectangle with sides BD and AD, area 1/2 × BC × AD.
items.answer: Cut along the altitude and join the two right triangles along their slanting sides to make a rectangle BD by AD

videos.answer: Cut along the altitude and join the two right triangles along their slanting sides to make a rectangle BD by AD

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 8)

items.question: [Śulba-Sūtras] Give a method to convert a rectangle into an isosceles triangle by dissection.
steps: Cut the rectangle along a diagonal into two congruent right triangles.
Flip one triangle over and stand the two back to back, joined along the leg equal to the width.
They form an isosceles triangle with base twice the rectangle's length and height equal to its width.
items.answer: Cut along a diagonal and stand the two right triangles back to back

videos.answer: Cut along a diagonal and stand the two right triangles back to back

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms, question 9)

items.question: Which has greater area: an equilateral triangle or a square of the same sidelength as the triangle? Which has greater area: two identical equilateral triangles together or a square of the same sidelength as the triangle? Give reasons.
steps: Square of side s: area s × s.
The triangle's height is less than its slanting side s, so its area is less than 1/2 × s × s.
Two triangles make a rhombus with base s and height less than s, so less than s × s too.
items.answer: The square is greater in both cases

videos.answer: The square is greater in both cases

source: A rhombus has diagonals 12 cm and 8 cm. Dissect it into a re

items.question: A rhombus has diagonals 12 cm and 8 cm. Dissect it into a rectangle and find the area.
steps: The rectangle has one side 12 cm, the whole diagonal.
Its other side is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm, half the other.
Area = 12 × 4 = 48 cm².
items.answer: 48 cm²

videos.answer: 48 cm²

source: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 6 cm. Find its area using

items.question: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 6 cm. Find its area using two triangles.
steps: Each triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
Each triangle: 1/2 × 10 × 3 = 15 cm².
Rhombus: 15 + 15 = 30 cm², and 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².
items.answer: 30 cm²

videos.answer: 30 cm²

source: Figure it Out (rhombus and trapezium, question 1)

items.question: Find the area of a rhombus whose diagonals are 20 cm and 15 cm.
items.answer: 150 cm²

videos.answer: 150 cm²

source: Figure it Out (rhombus and trapezium, question 2)

items.question: Give a method to convert a rectangle into a rhombus of equal area using dissection.
steps: Cut the rectangle (length L, width W) into two halves, each L/2 long and W wide.
Cut each half along a diagonal: four congruent right triangles with legs L/2 and W.
Arrange them with the right angles meeting at one centre point: a rhombus with diagonals L and 2W.

items.question: [Śulba-Sūtras] Give a method to convert an isosceles trapezium to a rectangle using dissection.
steps: Mark the midpoint of each slanting side.
Through each midpoint draw a line perpendicular to the parallel sides.
Cut off the small corner triangle below each midpoint and turn it about the midpoint into the gap above it; the two halves of each slanting side match.
The result is a rectangle with height h and length 1/2 × (a + b).
items.answer: Cut through the midpoints of the slanting sides at right angles to the base and swing the corner pieces up: a rectangle 1/2 × (a + b) by h

items.question: Here is one of the ways to convert trapezium ABCD into a rectangle EFGH of equal area. Given the trapezium ABCD, how do we find the vertices of the rectangle EFGH? (Hint: if ΔAHI ≅ ΔDGI and ΔBEJ ≅ ΔCFJ, then the trapezium and rectangle have equal areas.)
steps: Mark I and J, the midpoints of the slanting sides AD and BC.
Through I draw the line perpendicular to DC; it meets DC at G and the line AB extended at H.
Through J do the same to get F on DC and E on AB extended.
Since AI = DI and the angles match, ΔAHI ≅ ΔDGI and ΔBEJ ≅ ΔCFJ, so EFGH has the trapezium's area.
items.answer: Take the midpoints I and J of the slanting sides and draw perpendiculars to DC through them; they meet DC and line AB at G, H, F and E

items.question: ZYXW is a trapezium with ZY ∥ WX. A is the midpoint of XY. Show that the area of the trapezium ZYXW is equal to the area of ΔZWB, where ZA extended meets WX extended at B.
steps: YA = XA, since A is the midpoint of XY.
∠ZAY = ∠BAX (vertically opposite) and ∠ZYA = ∠BXA (alternate angles, since ZY ∥ WB).
So ΔZYA ≅ ΔBXA (ASA): they have equal areas.
Trapezium ZYXW = ZAXW + ΔZYA = ZAXW + ΔBXA = ΔZWB.
items.answer: ΔZYA ≅ ΔBXA, so swapping one for the other shows the trapezium and ΔZWB have equal areas
